title: Support-ticket triage service for a SaaS helpdesk
scenario: Brightdesk, a 30-person SaaS company, gets about 1,200 support tickets a day and two agents spend the morning hand-sorting them. They want automatic category, priority and suggested-team labels with a confidence score so low-confidence tickets still go to a human.

nonFunctional: p95 latency under 3 s per ticket
Macro-F1 of at least 0.80 on 500 held-out tickets
Cost under $15/month at 1,200 tickets/day
constraints: Hosted LLM API only, no fine-tuning
architecture: A FastAPI service wraps a prompt with a JSON schema, validates output, and logs every call. An offline eval harness replays a labeled set against each prompt version.
stack: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLite, an LLM API
data: Public customer-support/complaint text datasets (e.g. Consumer Financial Protection complaints, Bitext customer-support set) relabeled into 8 invented categories

milestones.step: Define label taxonomy and build 500-ticket labeled eval set
Eval harness with per-class report and prompt A/B

doneWhen: Macro-F1 >= 0.80 on the held-out set, p95 < 3 s, projected monthly cost < $15 shown in a cost table.
measure: Macro-F1, per-class confusion, p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tickets, invalid-JSON retry rate
pitfalls: Eval set leakage from few-shot examples
Label ambiguity inflating error; write labeling guide
stretch: Add active-learning loop that surfaces uncertain tickets
Compare against a TF-IDF + logistic regression baseline
